name: @projexlight/sdk-asset
summary: Digital-twin registry and sensor-telemetry plane for physical-AI fleets. A robot is modeled as an `asset` (linked to its device_uuid for enrollment/attestation), composed of a self-referential `component` tree (torso -> arm -> hand -> finger, leg, ...), where each component carries a `sensor` catalog. Per-sensor time-series land in `sensor_reading` (Postgres for dev, mirrored to ClickHouse at fleet scale) and are downsampled into 1-minute and 1-hour rollup tiers. registerAsset bulk-defines the whole twin in one transaction; getTwin rehydrates the nested tree; ingestReadings/queryReadings handle raw and rolled-up telemetry; and a background rollup job (backfill1m/rebuild1h/runSensorRollup) keeps the aggregate tiers current off the hot ingest path.

models.description: One row per registered robot/device (the digital-twin root): tenant_id + optional bu_id scoping, device_uuid linking to device.device for enrollment/attestation, model, display_name and status. Indexed by tenant_id and device_uuid.

Self-referential component tree for an asset (parent_component_id -> component_id, ON DELETE CASCADE): torso/head/arm/hand/finger/leg kinds with an optional name and jsonb position. Indexed by asset_id and parent_component_id.

Sensor catalog attached to a component (and denormalized asset_id): kind (force, temperature, joint_angle, camera, ...), unit and optional min_value/max_value/sample_rate_hz calibration bounds. CASCADE-deleted with its component/asset.

Per-sensor time-series readings keyed by (sensor_id, asset_id, tenant_id, ts, value, quality). Postgres-backed in dev and mirrored to ClickHouse at fleet scale with the same shape; source for the 1m/1h rollup tiers. Indexed by (sensor_id, ts DESC) and (asset_id, ts DESC).

scenarios.title: Register a robot and its component/sensor tree in one transaction
scenarios.when_to_use: When a new physical-AI unit is enrolled and you need to persist its full digital twin — the asset root plus a nested component hierarchy and each component's sensors — atomically.
scenarios.expected_outcome: The asset, its nested components and sensors are inserted in a single dataService.tx transaction; the call returns the new asset_id (or rolls the whole tree back on any failure).

scenarios.title: Rehydrate the full digital twin for inspection or a UI
scenarios.when_to_use: When a caller needs the complete asset -> nested components -> sensors structure, for example to render a twin viewer or validate a fleet unit's topology.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Returns a TwinNode with the asset fields and a reassembled component forest (each ComponentNode carrying its sensors and children), or null when the asset_id does not exist.

scenarios.title: Batch-ingest sensor readings and query a rolled-up view
scenarios.when_to_use: When streaming telemetry off a fleet unit and later reading it back either raw or aggregated per time bucket (second/minute/hour/day) for dashboards or anomaly checks.
scenarios.expected_outcome: ingestReadings returns { ingested: 2 }; queryReadings with a valid bucket returns per-bucket aggregates (n/min/max/avg/last), and without a bucket returns raw (ts, value, quality) rows, newest first (LIMIT 5000).

scenarios.title: Recompute rollup tiers for a replayed/backfilled window
scenarios.when_to_use: When historical or replayed telemetry the streaming materialized view never saw needs its 1m and 1h ClickHouse rollups rebuilt, off the hot ingest path. Requires initClickHouse() first.
scenarios.expected_outcome: runSensorRollup backfills the 1m tier from raw then rebuilds the 1h tier for the window (delete-then-reinsert, safe to re-run) and returns { rebuilt_1m: true, rebuilt_1h: true }; startSensorRollupJob returns a stop() that clears the interval.

compliance_posture.notes: All rows are tenant_id-scoped (with optional bu_id) so fleet twins and telemetry stay isolated per tenant. assets carry a device_uuid linking to device.device for enrollment/attestation rather than embedding credentials, and sensor_reading holds numeric measurements plus a quality flag — no PII — though high-volume telemetry is mirrored to ClickHouse and should inherit the same tenant-scoped retention controls.
